podcast.body: For their first album in 1980, Martin Gore and Vince Clark experimented by running their Korg and Roland synthesizers through a Big Muff pedal. This experimentation resulted in an instrumental track named after the pedal itself, "Big Muff," which highlighted the pedal's versatility beyond guitars. "Martin Gore and Vince Clark experimented with running their Corg and Roland synthesizers through a Big Muff. And the result was an instrumental by that same name."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in 1981, this was Depeche Mode's first album. It performed "all right" and featured a couple of hit singles, showcasing the band's distinctive new synthesizer sound. The album positioned the band on the cusp of a significant breakthrough in the music scene. "Depeche Mode's first album, Speaking Spell, did all right."

podcast.body: Vince Clarke practically composed, recorded, and produced this album almost entirely alone before leaving the band. His significant involvement laid the groundwork for the band's initial success. "el cual le había prácticamente insolitario compuesto grabado y producido."
